data.name: LdapConnectivityMissingValues
data.value: Unable to test connectivity due to missing directory server, port, username and/or password values
data.comment: Shown when the LDAP Connector's settings are saved without what it needs to connect.

data.name: LdapConnectivityFailed
data.value: Unable to connect. Message: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the error the directory or the network gave, in its own words (usually English).

data.name: LdapExchangeDirectoryTypeRefusal
data.value: Exchange recipients can be managed only on Active Directory, and this directory is {0}. Turn off {1}, or connect to an Active Directory domain controller.
data.comment: {0} is a directory kind (Samba AD, OpenLDAP, 389 Directory Server, or the phrase for one JIM does not recognise); {1} is the name of the Manage Exchange recipients setting, shown as that setting's label.

data.name: LdapDirectoryKindSambaAD
data.value: Samba AD
data.comment: A product name.

data.name: LdapDirectoryKindOpenLDAP
data.value: OpenLDAP
data.comment: A product name.

data.name: LdapDirectoryKindDirectoryServer389
data.value: 389 Directory Server
data.comment: A product name.

data.name: LdapDirectoryKindUnrecognised
data.value: not one JIM recognises
data.comment: Completes: this directory is ...

data.name: LdapExchangeRefusedRemotePowerShell
data.value: Exchange refused {0}: {1} The account signed in to the domain, but Exchange does not let it use remote PowerShell. Add it to Exchange's Recipient Management role group, and check its remote PowerShell access is not turned off.
data.comment: {0} is the account; {1} is what Exchange said, in its own words, ended as a sentence.

data.name: LdapExchangeUnreachable
data.value: JIM could not reach Exchange at {0}: {1} Check the Exchange server's name, and that this server can reach it on port {2}.
data.comment: {0} is the address; {1} is the network error in its own words, ended as a sentence; {2} is a port number.

data.name: LdapExchangeTimedOut
data.value: Exchange at {0} did not answer: {1} Check the server is running, and that nothing between this server and it is holding the connection.
data.comment: {0} is the address; {1} is the network error in its own words, ended as a sentence.

data.name: LdapExchangeCertificateUntrusted
data.value: JIM does not trust Exchange's certificate at {0}: {1} Add the certificate authority that issued it in Certificates, and use the server's name as its certificate gives it.
data.comment: {0} is the address; {1} is the error in its own words, ended as a sentence.

data.name: LdapExchangeSessionRefused
data.value: Exchange at {0} refused the session: {1}
data.comment: {1} is what Exchange said, in its own words.

data.name: LdapKerberosClockSkew
data.value: This server's clock differs from the domain's by more than five minutes, so Kerberos refused the sign-in. Correct the time on this server, or on the domain controller {0}, then save again.
data.comment: {0} is a domain controller's name.

data.name: LdapKerberosPasswordRefused
data.value: The domain refused the password for {0}. Check the Password above: JIM signs in to Exchange with the directory account.
data.comment: {0} is the account. "the Password above" refers to the Password setting.

data.name: LdapKerberosAccountUnknown
data.value: The domain controller {0} does not know the account {1}, so it cannot sign in to Exchange.
data.comment: {0} is a domain controller; {1} is the account.

data.name: LdapKerberosServiceUnknown
data.value: The domain has no service principal HTTP/{0}, so Kerberos cannot sign in to it. Use the Exchange server's own DNS name, not an alias or an IP address, as the Exchange server.
data.comment: {0} is a host name. "the Exchange server" refers to the Exchange server setting.

data.name: LdapKerberosAccountDisabled
data.value: The account {0} is disabled or locked out, so the domain refused the sign-in.
data.comment: {0} is the account.

data.name: LdapKerberosPasswordExpired
data.value: The account {0} cannot sign in because its password has expired. Set a new one, and enter it as the Password above.
data.comment: {0} is the account. "the Password above" refers to the Password setting.

data.name: LdapKerberosDomainControllerUnreachable
data.value: JIM could not reach the domain controller {0} on port 88 to sign in to Exchange with Kerberos. Check this server can reach it.
data.comment: {0} is a domain controller.

data.name: LdapKerberosRefused
data.value: Kerberos refused the sign-in for {0} through {1}: {2}
data.comment: {2} is the Kerberos library's own words.

data.name: LdapExchangeCommandsMissing
data.value: The account {0} cannot run {1} in Exchange, so JIM cannot manage these recipient types: {2}. Their changes will fail for insufficient permissions until it can. Add the account to Exchange's Recipient Management role group, or give it a role that includes those commands.
data.comment: {0} is the account; {1} is a list of Exchange command names; {2} is a comma-separated list of recipient types.

data.name: ListOr
data.comment: Joins the last two items of a list of command names; {0} is the earlier items already separated by commas.

data.name: LdapExchangeGetCommandFailed
data.value: JIM signed in to Exchange as {0}, but could not tell which commands the account may run, because Get-Command failed: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the account; {1} is the error in its own words.

data.name: GraphTenantAlias
data.value: '{0}' is a multi-tenant sign-in alias, not a tenant. Supply the tenant's ID (a GUID) or one of its verified domain names, shown as Directory (tenant) ID on the app registration's Overview page.
data.comment: {0} is what the administrator typed.

data.name: GraphTenantInvalid
data.value: The {0} must be the tenant's ID (a GUID) or one of its verified domain names, i.e. contoso.onmicrosoft.com. Supply the value on its own, not a sign-in URL.
data.comment: {0} is the Tenant ID setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: GraphClientIdInvalid
data.value: The {0} must be the app registration's Application (client) ID, a GUID such as 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, shown on its Overview page.
data.comment: {0} is the Client ID setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: GraphCloudUnknown
data.value: '{0}' is not a cloud this Connector knows. Choose one of: {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the value given; {1} is a comma-separated list of the clouds the Connector offers.

data.name: GraphNumberOutOfRange
data.value: {0} must be from {1} to {2}.
data.comment: {0} is a setting name; {1} and {2} are whole numbers. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: GraphManagedIdentityIdInvalid
data.value: The {0} must be the managed identity's client id, a GUID shown on its Overview page in the Azure portal.
data.comment: {0} is the setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: GraphSettingNotDecrypted
data.value: The {0} setting could not be decrypted.
data.comment: {0} is the setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: GraphTestRequestRefused
data.value: Authenticated, but Microsoft Graph refused the test request: {0}
data.comment: {0} is Microsoft Graph's own explanation.

data.name: GraphCouldNotConnect
data.value: Could not connect to Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft Graph. Check that JIM can reach them on HTTPS (port 443). Where a proxy inspects TLS traffic, add its CA certificate to JIM's certificate store under Admin > Certificates.
data.comment: Admin > Certificates is the portal's Certificates page.

data.name: EntraRefusedKnown
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID refused the token request (AADSTS{0}). {1}
data.comment: {0} is Entra ID's error number; {1} says what to do about it.

data.name: EntraRefusedWithDetail
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID refused the token request with HTTP {0} ({1}). Check the {2}, {3} and credential settings.
data.comment: {0} is an HTTP status number; {1} is Entra ID's error keyword and codes; {2} and {3} are setting names.

data.name: EntraRefusedWithStatus
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID refused the token request with HTTP {0}. Check the {1}, {2} and credential settings.
data.comment: {0} is an HTTP status number; {1} and {2} are setting names.

data.name: EntraSecretInvalid
data.value: The {0} is not valid. Supply the secret's Value from Certificates & secrets on the app registration, not its Secret ID.
data.comment: {0} is the Client Secret setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraSecretExpired
data.value: The {0} has expired. Create a new client secret on the app registration and supply it here.
data.comment: {0} is the Client Secret setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraApplicationNotFound
data.value: No application with this {0} was found in the tenant. Check the {0}, and that the app registration belongs to the tenant named in {1}.
data.comment: {0} is the Client ID setting's name; {1} is the Tenant ID setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraTenantNotFound
data.value: The tenant named in {0} was not found. Check it, and check the {1} setting: a tenant in a national cloud is not found on the global endpoints, nor the other way round.
data.comment: {0} is the Tenant ID setting's name; {1} is the Cloud setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraTenantIdInvalid
data.value: The {0} is not a valid tenant identifier. Supply the tenant's ID (a GUID) or one of its verified domain names.
data.comment: {0} is the Tenant ID setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraAssertionNotVerified
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID could not verify the assertion signed with the {0}. Check that the same certificate is uploaded under Certificates & secrets on the app registration. One uploaded in the last few minutes can still be refused while Entra ID applies it; if so, try again shortly.
data.comment: {0} is the Certificate setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraAssertionOutOfTime
data.value: The client assertion was outside its valid time range. Check that the clock on the JIM server is correct.

data.name: EntraApplicationDisabled
data.value: The application is disabled in the tenant. Enable its enterprise application (service principal) and try again.

data.name: EntraFederatedMismatch
data.value: The workload identity's token matches no federated credential on the app registration. Under Certificates & secrets > Federated credentials, add one for the managed identity named in {0}, for this cloud.
data.comment: {0} is the Managed Identity Client ID setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: EntraGraphNotFound
data.value: Microsoft Graph was not found in the tenant. Check that the {0} setting matches the cloud the tenant is in.
data.comment: {0} is the Cloud setting's name. A setting name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: ScimUrlInvalid
data.value: The '{0}' setting is not a valid absolute URL.
data.comment: {0} is a setting's name. A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: ScimUrlInvalidWithExample
data.value: The '{0}' setting is not a valid absolute URL. Supply the full address, i.e. {1}.
data.comment: {0} is a setting's name; {1} is an example address. A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: ScimUrlNotHttps
data.value: The '{0}' setting must use HTTPS. HTTP is only permitted for loopback addresses when testing locally, because {1} is sent to this address.
data.comment: {0} is a setting's name; {1} says what is sent there (a nested message). A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: ScimPayloadIdentityData
data.value: identity data
data.comment: What is sent to the SCIM service provider; completes: because ... is sent to this address.

data.name: ScimPayloadClientSecret
data.value: the Client Secret
data.comment: What is sent to the token endpoint; completes: because ... is sent to this address.

data.name: ScimNoDiscoveryAnswer
data.value: Connected to '{0}', but it did not answer on any SCIM discovery endpoint ({1}, {2} or {3}). Check the Base URL points at the root of the SCIM service, not at a resource endpoint such as /Users.
data.comment: {0} is the address; {1}, {2} and {3} are SCIM endpoint paths.

data.name: ScimCouldNotAuthenticate
data.value: Could not authenticate with the SCIM service provider: {0}
data.comment: {0} says why, as a message or the error's own words.

data.name: ScimCouldNotConnect
data.value: Could not connect to the SCIM service provider: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the network error in its own words.

data.name: SqlTimeZoneUnknown
data.value: {0} '{1}' is not a time zone this deployment recognises. Enter UTC, or an IANA time zone name such as Europe/London or America/New_York.
data.comment: {0} is the Database Time Zone setting's name; {1} is the value given. A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: SqlChooseDatabaseType
data.value: Choose a {0} before testing connectivity.
data.comment: {0} is the Database Type setting's name. A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: SqlMissingConnectionValues
data.value: Unable to test connectivity until {0}, {1} and {2} have been supplied.
data.comment: {0}, {1} and {2} are setting names (Host, Username, Password). A setting's name; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: SqlConnectFailed
data.value: Unable to connect. Message: {0}
data.comment: {0} is the database driver's own account of the failure.

data.name: FileNotFound
data.value: File not found: '{0}'. For {1} mode, the file must exist. Check the path and ensure it maps to a Docker Volume.
data.comment: {0} is the path; {1} is the mode, as the Mode setting stores it (Import Only, Bidirectional).

data.name: FileExportDirectoryNotCreated
data.value: Export directory could not be created: '{0}'. Error: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the directory; {1} is the system's own error.

data.name: CertServerScimServiceProvider
data.value: SCIM service provider
data.comment: A noun completing sentences about a certificate, e.g. 'Renew it on the ...'. French: masculine, no article; the sentence supplies it.

data.name: CertServerDirectoryServer
data.value: directory server
data.comment: A noun completing sentences about a certificate. French: masculine, no article.

data.name: CertServerDatabaseServer
data.value: database server
data.comment: A noun completing sentences about a certificate. French: masculine, no article.

data.name: CertNoCertificate
data.value: The {0} offered no certificate. Check that it is configured for {1} on this port.
data.comment: {0} is a server noun (a nested message); {1} is HTTPS, LDAPS, TCPS or TLS.

data.name: CertExpired
data.value: The certificate expired. Renew it on the {0}; trusting its issuer does not waive the expiry date.
data.comment: {0} is a server noun (a nested message).

data.name: CertNotYetValid
data.value: The certificate is not valid yet, which usually means the clocks on JIM and the {0} disagree.
data.comment: {0} is a server noun (a nested message).

data.name: CertNameMismatch
data.value: The certificate was not issued for '{0}'. Adding it to the JIM certificate store will not help; connect using a name the certificate carries, giving the JIM containers a host entry for it if that name cannot be resolved.
data.comment: {0} is the host name connected to.

data.name: CertChainProblem
data.value: {0} Trusting a certificate in JIM does not get past this; the certificate chain has to be fixed on the {1}.
data.comment: {0} is what is wrong with the chain (a nested message); {1} is a server noun (a nested message).

data.name: CertSelfSigned
data.value: The certificate is self-signed and not trusted. Add this certificate to the JIM certificate store (Admin > Certificates) to trust this {0}.
data.comment: {0} is a server noun (a nested message).

data.name: CertNothingTrustedWithRoot
data.value: Nothing in the certificate chain is trusted. Add '{0}', the root of the chain, to the JIM certificate store (Admin > Certificates) so that renewals of everything beneath it are trusted too. Any other certificate in the chain also works, until it is renewed.
data.comment: {0} is the root certificate's common name.

data.name: CertNothingTrustedIssuerMissing
data.value: Nothing in the certificate chain is trusted, and JIM could not find '{0}', the certificate authority that issued '{1}'. Trust a certificate JIM did find, or add '{0}' to the JIM certificate store (Admin > Certificates) so that renewals are trusted too.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are certificate common names.

data.name: CertRootNotTrusted
data.value: The root of the chain is not trusted. Add '{0}' to the JIM certificate store (Admin > Certificates). This connection accepts only the root: an intermediate or the {1}'s own certificate in the store does not make it work.
data.comment: {0} is the root certificate's common name; {1} is a server noun (a nested message).

data.name: CertRootNotTrustedIssuerMissing
data.value: The root of the chain is not trusted, and JIM could not find '{0}', the certificate authority above '{1}'. Get the root certificate from whoever runs your PKI and add it to the JIM certificate store (Admin > Certificates). This connection accepts only the root.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are certificate common names.

data.name: CertChainExpired
data.value: {0} expired on {1}. A chain through an expired certificate authority is never valid; it needs renewing.
data.comment: {0} is a certificate's name; {1} is a date.

data.name: CertChainNotYetValid
data.value: {0} is not valid until {1}.
data.comment: {0} is a certificate's name; {1} is a date.

data.name: CertChainNotAuthority
data.value: {0} is not marked as a certificate authority, so it cannot vouch for the certificate below it.
data.comment: {0} is a certificate's name.

data.name: CertChainBadSignature
data.value: The signature {0} made on the certificate below it does not verify.
data.comment: {0} is a certificate's name.

data.name: CertRejected
data.value: The {0}'s certificate was rejected: {1}
data.comment: {0} is a server noun (a nested message); {1} says why.

data.name: SqlDocObjectTypeNamed
data.value: Object Type '{0}'
data.comment: Mid-sentence reference to an Object Type of the SQL Connector's Object Types document. {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocObjectTypeNamedCapital
data.value: Object Type '{0}'
data.comment: The same, at the start of a sentence. {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocObjectTypeByPosition
data.value: the object type in position {0}
data.comment: Mid-sentence reference to an Object Type that has no name; {0} is its one-based position in the document.

data.name: SqlDocObjectTypeByPositionCapital
data.value: The object type in position {0}
data.comment: The same, at the start of a sentence.

data.name: SqlDocLevelColumn
data.value: A configured column of {0}
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type reference (a nested message).

data.name: SqlDocLevelRelatedTable
data.value: A related table of {0}
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type reference (a nested message).

data.name: SqlDocLevelChangeLog
data.value: The change log of {0}
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type reference (a nested message).

data.name: SqlDocLevelDocument
data.value: The {0} document
data.comment: {0} is the name of the Object Types setting; it is shown as that setting's label.

data.name: SqlDocUnrecognisedField
data.value: {0} has an unrecognised field '{1}'.{2} Fields that are not recognised are refused rather than ignored, because ignoring one would leave the Connected System configured differently from how the document reads.
data.comment: {0} says where the field is (a nested message); {1} is the field as written; {2} is empty or the suggestion (a nested message that starts with a space).

data.name: SqlDocDidYouMean
data.value: Did you mean '{0}'?
data.comment: Starts with a space: it follows a sentence. {0} is the field the administrator probably meant.

data.name: SqlDocJsonUnreadable
data.value: {0} could not be read as JSON: {1}
data.comment: {0} is the name of the Object Types setting; {1} is the JSON parser's own message.

data.name: SqlDocEmpty
data.value: {0} is empty. A Connected System needs at least one object type before JIM can discover its schema; see the setting's description for an example to start from.
data.comment: {0} is the name of the Object Types setting.

data.name: SqlDocNoObjectTypes
data.value: {0} must declare at least one object type in its 'objectTypes' list.
data.comment: {0} is the name of the Object Types setting. 'objectTypes' is a field of the JSON document and stays as written.

data.name: SqlDocDuplicateName
data.value: Object Type '{0}' is declared more than once. Object type names identify them to JIM, so each must be unique.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocPositionEmpty
data.value: The object type in position {0} of 'objectTypes' is empty.
data.comment: {0} is a one-based position.

data.name: SqlDocPositionNoName
data.value: The object type in position {0} of 'objectTypes' has no 'name'. Every object type needs one, because it is what JIM calls it.
data.comment: {0} is a one-based position.

data.name: SqlDocOneSource
data.value: Object Type '{0}' must name exactly one source: either a 'table' (a table or a view) or a 'select' statement, and not both.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocSchemaWithSelect
data.value: Object Type '{0}' supplies both a 'schema' and a 'select' statement. A schema qualifies a table name; a statement qualifies its own tables, so remove the 'schema'.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogAnchorCount
data.value: Object Type '{0}' identifies its change-log rows by {1} column(s), but the object type's anchor has {2}. A change attributed by part of an anchor belongs to some other object, so 'changeLog.anchorColumns' must name one column per anchor column, in the same order.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document. {1} and {2} are counts.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogAnchorDuplicate
data.value: Object Type '{0}' lists change-log anchor column '{1}' more than once.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogNoDelete
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has a change log with no 'deleteValues'. Observing deletions is what a change-log table is for; if this database cannot record them, use Watermark Column mode instead.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogNoCreateOrUpdate
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has a change log with neither 'createValues' nor 'updateValues', so nothing but deletions could ever be imported from it.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogEmptyValue
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has an empty value in 'changeLog.{1}'. A change-log row's change type is matched against these exactly, so a blank one could never match.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document. {1} is a field name.

data.name: SqlDocChangeLogValueAmbiguous
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has change-log value '{1}' meaning both {2} and {3}. Each value can only mean one kind of change.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document. {2} and {3} are kinds of change as the document names them.

data.name: SqlDocDeltaNeedsChangeLog
data.value: {0} is '{1}', but Object Type '{2}' is selected for synchronisation and has no 'changeLog'. A Delta Import that skipped an object type would report success while leaving its objects to drift, so every selected object type needs one. Give it a 'changeLog', or deselect it if JIM never imports from it.
data.comment: {0} is the Delta Import Mode setting's name; {1} is its value.

data.name: SqlDocDeltaNeedsWatermark
data.value: {0} is '{1}', but Object Type '{2}' is selected for synchronisation and has no 'watermarkColumn'. A Delta Import that skipped an object type would report success while leaving its objects to drift, so every selected object type needs one. Give it a 'watermarkColumn', or deselect it if JIM never imports from it.
data.comment: {0} is the Delta Import Mode setting's name; {1} is its value.

data.name: SqlDocRelatedNeedsWatermark
data.value: {0} is '{1}', but Object Type '{2}' has related table attribute '{3}' with no 'watermarkColumn'. A row added to or removed from '{4}' changes the object without touching its own row, so without a watermark column on the related table that change could never be detected.
data.comment: {0} is the Delta Import Mode setting's name; {1} is its value; {4} is a table name.

data.name: SqlDocNoAnchorColumns
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has no 'anchorColumns'. JIM identifies an object by its anchor, so at least one column must be named.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocAnchorDuplicate
data.value: Object Type '{0}' lists anchor column '{1}' more than once.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocColumnNoReference
data.value: Object Type '{0}' configures column '{1}' without a 'referencesObjectType'. A column is only configured to say what its type cannot, which today means naming the object type it points at.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocColumnDuplicate
data.value: Object Type '{0}' configures column '{1}' more than once.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocRelatedNoAttributeName
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has a related table with no 'attributeName'. The attribute name is what the multi-valued attribute is called on the object type.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocRelatedDuplicate
data.value: Object Type '{0}' declares related table attribute '{1}' more than once.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocJoinColumnCount
data.value: Object Type '{0}' joins related table attribute '{1}' on {2} column(s), but the object type's anchor has {3}. Joining on part of an anchor gathers another object's values onto this one, so 'joinColumns' must name one column per anchor column, in the same order.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document. {2} and {3} are counts.

data.name: SqlDocColumnReferenceUnknown
data.value: Object Type '{0}' says column '{1}' references object type '{2}', which this document does not declare. A reference can only point at an object type JIM also synchronises.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocRelatedReferenceUnknown
data.value: Object Type '{0}' says related table attribute '{1}' references object type '{2}', which this document does not declare.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocNoValueForField
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has no value for '{1}'.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocIdentifierWhitespace
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has '{1}' set to '{2}', which starts or ends with whitespace. Database identifiers are used exactly as written, so the spaces would name a different object.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocIdentifierInvalid
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has '{1}' set to a value that cannot name a database object: {2}
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document. {2} is the reason, in its own words.

data.name: SqlDocSelectNotQuery
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has a 'select' that does not begin with SELECT or WITH. JIM reads objects with it, so it has to be a query.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: SqlDocSelectSemicolon
data.value: Object Type '{0}' has a 'select' containing a semicolon. It must be a single statement, with no terminator.
data.comment: {0} is an Object Type's name as written in the document.

data.name: PfEncrypted
data.value: The connection is encrypted, so passwords are protected in transit.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfEnableSecureConnection
data.value: Enable the 'Use Secure Connection' setting on this Connected System, and set the port to the one the directory serves LDAPS on.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. 'Use Secure Connection' is the LDAP Connector's setting.

data.name: PfAdRefusesUnencrypted
data.value: Active Directory refuses to accept a password over a connection that is neither encrypted nor signed and sealed, so a password set is likely to be rejected until this is addressed.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfNotEncrypted
data.value: The connection is not encrypted. Passwords would be sent where anyone on the network path can read them.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfMechanismAd
data.value: JIM would set passwords by writing the '{0}' attribute, which is how Active Directory accepts them.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is an LDAP attribute name.

data.name: PfMechanismPasswordModify
data.value: JIM would set passwords using the LDAP Password Modify extended operation, which this directory advertises support for.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfMechanismUnsupported
data.value: This directory does not advertise the LDAP Password Modify extended operation, which is the only mechanism JIM will use to set a password on a directory that is not Active Directory.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfMechanismLooksFor
data.value: JIM looks for the extended operation '{0}' on the directory's rootDSE.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is an object identifier.

data.name: PfMechanismNoDirectWrite
data.value: JIM will not write a password attribute directly instead, because a directory stores a directly written value exactly as given rather than hashing it, which would leave cleartext passwords in the directory.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsNotCheckable
data.value: JIM cannot check whether the account it connects as is allowed to reset passwords on this directory.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsNotCheckableDetail
data.value: This directory publishes no way for a client to ask what it is allowed to do, so the account's rights have to be confirmed at the directory itself.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsNoContainers
data.value: JIM cannot check whether the account it connects as is allowed to reset passwords, because it does not yet know where it would be provisioning.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsSelectContainers
data.value: Select the containers to manage on the Scope tab, then check again.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. The Scope tab is the Connected System's tab of that name.

data.name: PfRightsFinding
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is an outcome (a nested message); {1} is a container's distinguished name; {2} is the finding's detail, in its own words.

data.name: PfOutcomeAllowed
data.value: Allowed in
data.comment: Completes a line naming a container; the container follows.

data.name: PfOutcomeDenied
data.value: Not allowed in
data.comment: Completes a line naming a container; the container follows.

data.name: PfOutcomeUnknown
data.value: Could not tell for
data.comment: Completes a line naming a container; the container follows.

data.name: PfRightsCheckedFirst
data.value: JIM checked the first {0} of this Connected System's {1} managed containers.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} and {1} are counts.

data.name: PfRightsDenied
data.value: The account JIM connects as cannot reset passwords everywhere it would be provisioning.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsUnconfirmed
data.value: JIM could not confirm everywhere that the account it connects as is allowed to reset passwords.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfRightsAllowed
data.value: The account JIM connects as can reset passwords everywhere it would be provisioning.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyNounDomain
data.value: the domain password policy
data.comment: Completes: JIM could not read ... Feminine in French.

data.name: PfPolicyNounDirectory
data.value: the directory's password policy
data.comment: Completes: JIM could not read ... Feminine in French.

data.name: PfPolicyUnreadable
data.value: JIM could not read {0}, so it cannot pre-fill the password generator from it.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a policy noun (a nested message), feminine in French.

data.name: PfPolicyRead
data.value: JIM read {0} and can pre-fill the password generator from it.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a policy noun (a nested message), feminine in French.

data.name: PfPolicyRemedyActiveDirectory
data.value: Check that the account JIM connects as can read the domain root object.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyRemedyOpenLdap
data.value: Check that the account JIM connects as can read the policy entry the ppolicy overlay applies by default.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyRemedyDirectoryServer389
data.value: Check that the account JIM connects as can read the password attributes on cn=config.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyRemedyOther
data.value: Check that the account JIM connects as can read where this directory holds its password policy.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyNotPublished
data.value: This directory does not publish a password policy that a client can read, so JIM cannot pre-fill the password generator from it.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyConfigNotReadable
data.value: JIM could not read the directory's password policy: the account it connects as cannot read the server configuration that holds it.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfConfigRemedyOpenLdap
data.value: Grant the account JIM connects as read access to the ppolicy overlay configuration under cn=config and to the policy entry it names, then check again.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfConfigRemedyDirectoryServer389
data.value: Grant the account JIM connects as read access to the password attributes on cn=config, then check again.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfConfigRemedyOther
data.value: Grant the account JIM connects as read access to the server configuration that holds the password policy, then check again.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPolicyNoneConfigured
data.value: JIM read the directory's password policy configuration: no policy is configured, so no rules apply to a generated password.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfMinimumLength
data.value: Minimum length: {0}.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a number of characters.

data.name: PfComplexityRequired
data.value: Complexity is required: a password must use at least {0} of the 5 character categories.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a number.

data.name: PfComplexityNotRequired
data.value: Complexity is not required.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfPpolicyNotLoaded
data.value: The directory does not advertise the password policy control, so the ppolicy overlay is not loaded.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfSetByHand
data.value: Set the password requirements on the Synchronisation Rule to match the target's policy by hand, and expect a rejection to be how a mismatch shows up.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfFgppPresent
data.value: This domain has Fine-Grained Password Policies, which apply stricter rules to some accounts. What JIM read is a floor, not the whole story.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfOverridePresent
data.value: Some objects in this directory are governed by a password policy other than the one JIM read, which may be stricter. What JIM read is a floor, not the whole story.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfFgppUnknown
data.value: JIM could not establish whether this domain has Fine-Grained Password Policies, which would apply stricter rules to some accounts. Treat what it read as a floor.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfOverrideUnknown
data.value: JIM could not establish whether some objects in this directory are governed by a password policy other than the one it read, which could be stricter. Treat what it read as a floor.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfFurtherChecks
data.value: The directory applies further checks JIM cannot see, so a password satisfying everything above can still be refused.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphNoToken
data.value: No access token could be acquired from Microsoft Entra ID: {0}
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is the error in its own words.

data.name: PfGraphHttps
data.value: Microsoft Graph is reached over HTTPS, with TLS 1.2 or later.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfNotChecked
data.value: Not checked: no connection.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphPolicySame
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID's password rules are the same in every tenant.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphToken
data.value: An access token was acquired from Microsoft Entra ID.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphMechanism
data.value: Passwords are set through Microsoft Graph, on the user's passwordProfile.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphPolicySameBanned
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID's password rules are the same in every tenant; its banned password list cannot be read.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.

data.name: PfGraphLacksPermission
data.value: The app registration lacks the {0} application permission. Grant it with admin consent.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a Microsoft Graph permission name.

data.name: PfGraphHoldsRole
data.value: The app holds the permission and the {0} directory role across the tenant.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab. {0} is a Microsoft Entra directory role name.

data.name: PfGraphNoRole
data.value: The app holds the permission, but its token shows no directory role that resets passwords. Graph also needs the app to hold User Administrator across the tenant: run Register-JIMEntraIdConnector -PasswordManagement, or assign it in the Entra admin centre. A role assigned in the last hour can be missing from the token until it is renewed.
data.comment: A line of the password preflight report shown on the Connected System's Passwords tab.
